q: A nutrient cycle is a repeated pathway of a particular nutrient or element from the physical environment to living organisms and back to the environment.
e: True. A nutrient cycle is a repeated pathway of a particular nutrient or element from the physical environment to living organisms and back to the environment. Biological molecules occur naturally inside living organisms, not in bare rock. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic.

q: The six main nutrient cycles of an ecosystem are carbon cycle, hydrogen cycle, oxygen cycle, nitrogen cycle, phosphorous cycle and sulphur cycle.
e: True. The six main nutrient cycles of an ecosystem are carbon cycle, hydrogen cycle, oxygen cycle, nitrogen cycle, phosphorous cycle and sulphur cycle. The nitrogen cycle depends on fixing, nitrifying, and denitrifying microbes. The nitrogen cycle moves nitrogen between air, soil, microbes, and living tissue.

q: Nitrogen gas constitutes 78% of the atmosphere.
e: True. Nitrogen gas constitutes 78% of the atmosphere. The atmosphere is the layer of gases around the earth. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule.

q: The $N_2$ gas is inert and unable to be used by plants and animals.
e: True. The N2 gas is inert and unable to be used by plants and animals.

q: Nitrogen cycle consists of four main steps: Nitrogen fixation, ammonification, nitrification, and denitrification.
e: True. Nitrogen cycle consists of four main steps: Nitrogen fixation, ammonification, nitrification, and denitrification. The nitrogen cycle depends on fixing, nitrifying, and denitrifying microbes. The nitrogen cycle moves nitrogen between air, soil, microbes, and living tissue.

q: The first stage of the nitrogen cycle is the conversion of inert nitrogen gas ($N_2$) into ammonia ($NH_3$).
e: True. The first stage of the nitrogen cycle is the conversion of inert nitrogen gas (N2) into ammonia (NH3). The nitrogen cycle depends on fixing, nitrifying, and denitrifying microbes. The nitrogen cycle moves nitrogen between air, soil, microbes, and living tissue.

q: Nitrogen fixation is catalysed by the enzyme nitrogenase, which is produced by nitrogen-fixing bacteria in the soil.
e: True. Nitrogen fixation is catalysed by the enzyme nitrogenase, which is produced by nitrogen-fixing bacteria in the soil. Nitrogenase is the enzyme that fixes nitrogen gas into a usable form. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule.

q: Azotobacter forms a mutualistic association with the roots of legumes, while Rhizobium is found living freely in the soil.
e: False. It is not true that azotobacter forms a mutualistic association with the roots of legumes, while Rhizobium is found living freely in the soil. Azotobacter is a free-living nitrogen-fixing bacterium. Legumes host nitrogen-fixing Rhizobium in root nodules.

q: Rhizobium forms nodules within the plant roots and supplies ammonia to the plant in exchange for carbohydrates.
e: True. Rhizobium forms nodules within the plant roots and supplies ammonia to the plant in exchange for carbohydrates. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure. Roots may use air spaces or aerenchyma when soil oxygen is low.

q: Ammonia ($NH_3$) becomes ammonium ($NH_4^+$) when mixed with water, and this can be used by plants.
e: True. Ammonia (NH3) becomes ammonium (NH4^+) when mixed with water, and this can be used by plants. Ammonium is a form of nitrogen plants can take up after ammonification or fixation.

q: The process by which saprotrophs decompose organic materials to produce ammonia is known as nitrification.
e: False. It is not true that the process by which saprotrophs decompose organic materials to produce ammonia is known as nitrification. Saprotrophs digest dead organic matter outside their cells, then absorb it. Organic biological molecules all contain carbon.

q: Nitrification is the conversion of ammonium ions into nitrites ($NO_2^-$) and nitrates ($NO_3^-$) by nitrifying bacteria in the soil.
e: True. Nitrification is the conversion of ammonium ions into nitrites (NO2^-) and nitrates (NO3^-) by nitrifying bacteria in the soil. Nitrites are the middle step as ammonia is oxidised toward nitrate. Ammonium is a form of nitrogen plants can take up after ammonification or fixation.

q: Nitrosomonas converts nitrites into nitrates, while Nitrobacter converts ammonium ions into nitrites.
e: False. It is not true that nitrosomonas converts nitrites into nitrates, while Nitrobacter converts ammonium ions into nitrites. Nitrosomonas oxidises ammonia to nitrite in nitrification. Nitrites are the middle step as ammonia is oxidised toward nitrate.

q: Nitrification reactions require oxygen and hence soil must be well aerated to ensure a rich supply of nitrites and nitrates.
e: True. Nitrification reactions require oxygen and hence soil must be well aerated to ensure a rich supply of nitrites and nitrates. Nitrites are the middle step as ammonia is oxidised toward nitrate.

q: Denitrification is a chemical reduction process that converts nitrates ($NO_3^-$) into nitrogen gas ($N_2$).
e: True. Denitrification is a chemical reduction process that converts nitrates (NO3^-) into nitrogen gas (N2). Chromosome number is reduced in meiosis I, not in mitosis. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule.

q: Denitrification is carried out by denitrifying bacteria in the presence of oxygen.
e: False. It is not true that denitrification is carried out by denitrifying bacteria in the presence of oxygen.

q: Phosphorus is a component of biological molecules such as RNA, DNA, phospholipids, and adenosine triphosphate (ATP).
e: True. Phosphorus is a component of biological molecules such as RNA, DNA, phospholipids, and adenosine triphosphate (ATP). ATP is the cell's immediate energy currency. DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides.

q: Phosphorus cycle is a very fast process.
e: False. Phosphorus cycle is not a very fast process.

q: Phosphorus is found in rocks and comes out from the rocks by weathering.
e: True. Phosphorus is found in rocks and comes out from the rocks by weathering. Weathering of rock releases mineral nutrients into soil. Rocks and soil belong to the lithosphere.

q: Sulphur is an essential component of living organisms and is a constituent part of many proteins and enzyme cofactors.
e: True. Sulphur is an essential component of living organisms and is a constituent part of many proteins and enzyme cofactors. Biological molecules occur naturally inside living organisms, not in bare rock. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs.

q: When fossil fuels are burnt, sulphur is released as sulphur dioxide ($SO_2$).
e: True. When fossil fuels are burnt, sulphur is released as sulphur dioxide (SO2).

q: Sulphur dioxide is one of the main components of acid rain.
e: True. Sulphur dioxide is one of the main components of acid rain.
